title: The Old Man Lost His Horse
synopsis: The story of an old man from the frontier who lost his horse is often used in Chinese to express the idea of a "silver lining" or "blessing in disguise".

fullText.simplified:
塞翁失马

    很久以前，有一位老大爷，带着儿子住在中国的边塞地区，父子两人生活得很平静。
    一天，老大爷家里养的马突然自己跑出去，跑到了对面的国家，很难再找回来了。邻居们听说了这件事，都来陪老大爷聊天，希望他不要难过。令大家没想到的是，老大爷笑了，说：“谁说这一定是坏事呢？”
    几个月后，老大爷家的马自己回家了，还带回了一匹塞外的好马。这下邻居们吃惊极了，又都来到老大爷家，祝贺他得到了一匹好马。这一次，老大爷还是只笑了一下，说：“唉，这可不一定是幸运的事啊！”但大家还是很羡慕他的好运气。
    接下来的几个月，老大爷的儿子很高兴。塞外的马跑得比家里的快，儿子喜欢极了，每天出门都会骑这匹塞外好马。可突然有一天，儿子从马背上摔了下来，把大腿摔断了，从此以后都不能骑马了。邻居们觉得太可惜了，劝老大爷不要难过。老大爷还是只笑了一下，“这可能是个礼物啊！”
    到了年底，塞外人南下，边塞打仗了，政府开始征兵。老大爷的儿子因为摔断了腿，不能当兵，被留在了家里。几年过去了，塞外人终于被打回去了，但政府这边去打仗的很多兵都死了。老大爷的儿子虽然断了一条腿，却得到了活下来的机会。
    塞翁失马焉知非福，是一个中国人常用的成语。意思是每件事情都有两面性，遇到坏事不要太难过，遇到好事也别骄傲。下次朋友遇到不好的事时，就可以告诉他：“塞翁失马，也许明天会有好事发生，笑一下！”
fullText.traditional:
塞翁失馬

    很久以前，有一位老大爺，帶著兒子住在中國的邊塞地區，父子兩人生活得很平靜。
    一天，老大爺家裡養的馬突然自己跑出去，跑到了對面的國家，很難再找回來了。鄰居們聽說了這件事，都來陪老大爺聊天，希望他不要難過。令大家沒想到的是，老大爺笑了，說：“誰說這一定是壞事呢？”
    幾個月後，老大爺家的馬自己回家了，還帶回了一匹塞外的好馬。這下鄰居們吃驚極了，又都來到老大爺家，祝賀他得到了一匹好馬。這一次，老大爺還是只笑了一下，說：“唉，這可不一定是幸運的事啊！”但大家還是很羨慕他的好運氣。
    接下來的幾個月，老大爺的兒子很高興。塞外的馬跑得比家裡的快，兒子喜歡極了，每天出門都會騎這匹塞外好馬。可突然有一天，兒子從馬背上摔了下來，把大腿摔斷了，從此以後都不能騎馬了。鄰居們覺得太可惜了，勸老大爺不要難過。老大爺還是只笑了一下，“這可能是個禮物啊！”
    到了年底，塞外人南下，邊塞打仗了，政府開始徵兵。老大爺的兒子因為摔斷了腿，不能當兵，被留在了家裡。幾年過去了，塞外人終於被打回去了，但政府這邊去打仗的很多兵都死了。老大爺的兒子雖然斷了一條腿，卻得到了活下來的機會。
    塞翁失馬焉知非福，是一個中國人常用的成語。意思是每件事情都有兩面性，遇到壞事不要太難過，遇到好事也別驕傲。下次朋友遇到不好的事時，就可以告訴他：“塞翁失馬，也許明天會有好事發生，笑一下！”

sentences.english: The Old Man Lost His Horse

sentences.simplified: 很久以前，有一位老大爷，带着儿子住在中国的边塞地区，
sentences.traditional: 很久以前，有一位老大爺，帶著兒子住在中國的邊塞地區，
sentences.pinyin: hěn jiǔ yǐ qián yǒu yí wèi lǎo dà yé dài zhe ér zi zhù zài zhōng guó de biān sài dì qū

sentences.simplified: 父子两人生活得很平静。
sentences.traditional: 父子兩人生活得很平靜。
sentences.pinyin: fù zǐ liǎng rén shēng huó de hěn píng jìng
sentences.english: A long time ago, there was an old man who took his son to live on the frontier of China.
The father and son lived a very peaceful life.

sentences.simplified: 一天，老大爷家里养的马突然自己跑出去，
sentences.traditional: 一天，老大爺家裡養的馬突然自己跑出去，
sentences.pinyin: yì tiān lǎo dà yé jiā lǐ yǎng de mǎ tū rán zì jǐ pǎo chū qù

sentences.simplified: 跑到了对面的国家，很难再找回来了。
sentences.traditional: 跑到了對面的國家，很難再找回來了。
sentences.pinyin: pǎo dào le duì miàn de guó jiā hěn nán zài zhǎo huí lai le
sentences.english: One day, the old man’s horse suddenly ran away from home.

sentences.simplified: 邻居们听说了这件事，都来陪老大爷聊天，希望他不要难过。
sentences.traditional: 鄰居們聽說了這件事，都來陪老大爺聊天，希望他不要難過。
sentences.pinyin: lín jū men tīng shuō le zhè jiàn shì dōu lái péi lǎo dà yé liáo tiān xī wàng tā bú yào nán guò
sentences.english: It escaped to the neighboring country, making it very difficult to find and bring it back again.

sentences.simplified: 令大家没想到的是，老大爷笑了，说：“谁说这一定是坏事呢？”
sentences.traditional: 令大家沒想到的是，老大爺笑了，說：“誰說這一定是壞事呢？”
sentences.pinyin: lìng dà jiā méi xiǎng dào de shì lǎo dà yé xiào le shuō shéi shuō zhè yí dìng shì huài shì ne
sentences.english: The neighbors, having heard about this, all came to keep to the old man company and chat with him, hoping he wouldn’t feel too upset.
They hadn’t expected that the old man would laugh and say, “Who said this must be a bad thing?”

sentences.simplified: 几个月后，老大爷家的马自己回家了，还带回了一匹塞外的好马。
sentences.traditional: 幾個月後，老大爺家的馬自己回家了，還帶回了一匹塞外的好馬。
sentences.pinyin: jǐ ge yuè hòu lǎo dà yé jiā de mǎ zì jǐ huí jiā le hái dài huí le yì pǐ sài wài de hǎo mǎ

sentences.simplified: 这下邻居们吃惊极了，
sentences.traditional: 這下鄰居們吃驚極了，
sentences.pinyin: zhè xià lín jū men chī jīng jí le
sentences.english: A few months later, the old man’s horse came back on its own, bringing with it a fine horse from beyond the frontier.

sentences.simplified: 又都来到老大爷家，祝贺他得到了一匹好马。
sentences.traditional: 又都來到老大爺家，祝賀他得到了一匹好馬。
sentences.pinyin: yòu dōu lái dào lǎo dà yé jiā zhù hè tā dé dào le yì pǐ hǎo mǎ
sentences.english: This time, the neighbors were extremely surprised.

sentences.simplified: 这一次，老大爷还是只笑了一下，说：“唉，这可不一定是幸运的事啊！”
sentences.traditional: 這一次，老大爺還是只笑了一下，說：“唉，這可不一定是幸運的事啊！”
sentences.pinyin: zhè yí cì lǎo dà yé hái shi zhǐ xiào le yí xià shuō ài zhè kě bù yí dìng shì xìng yùn de shì a
sentences.english: They all came to the old man’s house again to congratulate him on getting a fine horse.

sentences.simplified: 但大家还是很羡慕他的好运气。
sentences.traditional: 但大家還是很羨慕他的好運氣。
sentences.pinyin: dàn dà jiā hái shi hěn xiàn mù tā de hǎo yùn qi
sentences.english: This time, the old man still just smiled and said, “Ah, this may not necessarily be a lucky thing!”
But everyone was still very envious of his good luck.

sentences.simplified: 接下来的几个月，老大爷的儿子很高兴。
sentences.traditional: 接下來的幾個月，老大爺的兒子很高興。
sentences.pinyin: jiē xià lái de jǐ ge yuè lǎo dà yé de ér zi hěn gāo xìng

sentences.simplified: 塞外的马跑得比家里的快，儿子喜欢极了，
sentences.traditional: 塞外的馬跑得比家裡的快，兒子喜歡極了，
sentences.pinyin: sài wài de mǎ pǎo de bǐ jiā lǐ de kuài ér zi xǐ huan jí le
sentences.english: In the following months, the old man’s son was very happy.

sentences.simplified: 每天出门都会骑这匹塞外好马。
sentences.traditional: 每天出門都會騎這匹塞外好馬。
sentences.pinyin: měi tiān chū mén dōu huì qí zhè pǐ sài wài hǎo mǎ
sentences.english: The horse from beyond the frontier ran faster than the one from home, and the son really liked this horse.

sentences.simplified: 可突然有一天，儿子从马背上摔了下来，把大腿摔断了，从此以后都不能骑马了。
sentences.traditional: 可突然有一天，兒子從馬背上摔了下來，把大腿摔斷了，從此以後都不能騎馬了。
sentences.pinyin: kě tū rán yǒu yì tiān ér zi cóng mǎ bèi shang shuāi le xià lái bǎ dà tuǐ shuāi duàn le cóng cǐ yǐ hòu dōu bù néng qí mǎ le
sentences.english: Every day when he went out he would ride this fine horse from beyond the frontier.

sentences.simplified: 邻居们觉得太可惜了，劝老大爷不要难过。
sentences.traditional: 鄰居們覺得太可惜了，勸老大爺不要難過。
sentences.pinyin: lín jū men jué de tài kě xī le quàn lǎo dà yé bú yào nán guò
sentences.english: But suddenly one day, the son fell off the horse’s back and broke his leg. From then on, he could no longer ride a horse.

sentences.simplified: 老大爷还是只笑了一下，“这可能是个礼物啊！”
sentences.traditional: 老大爺還是只笑了一下，“這可能是個禮物啊！”
sentences.pinyin: lǎo dà yé hái shi zhǐ xiào le yí xià zhè kě néng shì ge lǐ wù a
sentences.english: The neighbors thought that this was too unfortunate, and tried to persuade the old man not to be sad.
The old man still just smiled: “This might be a gift!”

sentences.simplified: 到了年底，塞外人南下，
sentences.traditional: 到了年底，塞外人南下，
sentences.pinyin: dào le nián dǐ sài wài rén nán xià

sentences.simplified: 边塞打仗了，政府开始征兵。
sentences.traditional: 邊塞打仗了，政府開始徵兵。
sentences.pinyin: biān sài dǎ zhàng le zhèng fǔ kāi shǐ zhēng bīng
sentences.english: At the end of the year, people from beyond the frontier moved southward.

sentences.simplified: 老大爷的儿子因为摔断了腿，不能当兵，被留在了家里。
sentences.traditional: 老大爺的兒子因為摔斷了腿，不能當兵，被留在了家裡。
sentences.pinyin: lǎo dà yé de ér zi yīn wèi shuāi duàn le tuǐ bù néng dāng bīng bèi liú zài le jiā lǐ
sentences.english: Fighting broke out at the frontier, and the government began conscripting soldiers.

sentences.simplified: 几年过去了，塞外人终于被打回去了，
sentences.traditional: 幾年過去了，塞外人終於被打回去了，
sentences.pinyin: jǐ nián guò qù le sài wài rén zhōng yú bèi dǎ huí qu le
sentences.english: Because the old man’s son had broken his leg, he couldn’t join the army and was left at home.

sentences.simplified: 但政府这边去打仗的很多兵都死了。
sentences.traditional: 但政府這邊去打仗的很多兵都死了。
sentences.pinyin: dàn zhèng fǔ zhè biān qù dǎ zhàng de hěn duō bīng dōu sǐ le
sentences.english: Several years passed, and the people from beyond the frontier had finally been driven back.

sentences.simplified: 老大爷的儿子虽然断了一条腿，却得到了活下来的机会。
sentences.traditional: 老大爺的兒子雖然斷了一條腿，卻得到了活下來的機會。
sentences.pinyin: lǎo dà yé de ér zi suī rán duàn le yì tiáo tuǐ què dé dào le huó xià lai de jī huì
sentences.english: But many soldiers who went to fight for the government had died.
Although the old man’s son had broken a leg, he got a chance to survive.

sentences.simplified: 塞翁失马焉知非福，是一个中国人常用的成语。
sentences.traditional: 塞翁失馬焉知非福，是一個中國人常用的成語。
sentences.pinyin: sài wēng shī mǎ yān zhī fēi fú shì yí ge zhōng guó rén cháng yòng de chéng yǔ

sentences.simplified: 意思是每件事情都有两面性，遇到坏事不要太难过，遇到好事也别骄傲。
sentences.traditional: 意思是每件事情都有兩面性，遇到壞事不要太難過，遇到好事也別驕傲。
sentences.pinyin: yì si shì měi jiàn shì qing dōu yǒu liǎng miàn xìng yù dào huài shì bú yào tài nán guò yù dào hǎo shì yě bié jiāo ào
sentences.english: “The old man lost his horse, but it all turned out for the best” is an idiom often used by Chinese people.

sentences.simplified: 下次朋友遇到不好的事时，就可以告诉他：
sentences.traditional: 下次朋友遇到不好的事時，就可以告訴他：
sentences.pinyin: xià cì péng you yù dào bù hǎo de shì shí jiù kě yǐ gào su tā
sentences.english: The meaning is that everything has two sides. Don’t be too sad when bad things happen, and don’t be arrogant when good things happen.

sentences.simplified: “塞翁失马，也许明天会有好事发生，笑一下！”
sentences.traditional: “塞翁失馬，也許明天會有好事發生，笑一下！”
sentences.pinyin: sài wēng shī mǎ yě xǔ míng tiān huì yǒu hǎo shì fā shēng xiào yí xià
sentences.english: Next time something bad happens to a friend, you can tell your friend:

sentence_translations: The Old Man Lost His Horse
A long time ago, there was an old man who took his son to live on the frontier of China.
The father and son lived a very peaceful life.
One day, the old man’s horse suddenly ran away from home.
It escaped to the neighboring country, making it very difficult to find and bring it back again.
The neighbors, having heard about this, all came to keep to the old man company and chat with him, hoping he wouldn’t feel too upset.
They hadn’t expected that the old man would laugh and say, “Who said this must be a bad thing?”
A few months later, the old man’s horse came back on its own, bringing with it a fine horse from beyond the frontier.
This time, the neighbors were extremely surprised.
They all came to the old man’s house again to congratulate him on getting a fine horse.
This time, the old man still just smiled and said, “Ah, this may not necessarily be a lucky thing!”
But everyone was still very envious of his good luck.
In the following months, the old man’s son was very happy.
The horse from beyond the frontier ran faster than the one from home, and the son really liked this horse.
Every day when he went out he would ride this fine horse from beyond the frontier.
But suddenly one day, the son fell off the horse’s back and broke his leg. From then on, he could no longer ride a horse.
The neighbors thought that this was too unfortunate, and tried to persuade the old man not to be sad.
The old man still just smiled: “This might be a gift!”
At the end of the year, people from beyond the frontier moved southward.
Fighting broke out at the frontier, and the government began conscripting soldiers.
Because the old man’s son had broken his leg, he couldn’t join the army and was left at home.
Several years passed, and the people from beyond the frontier had finally been driven back.
But many soldiers who went to fight for the government had died.
Although the old man’s son had broken a leg, he got a chance to survive.
“The old man lost his horse, but it all turned out for the best” is an idiom often used by Chinese people.
The meaning is that everything has two sides. Don’t be too sad when bad things happen, and don’t be arrogant when good things happen.
Next time something bad happens to a friend, you can tell your friend:
“The old man lost his horse. Perhaps something good will happen tomorrow. Smile!”
